newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may barter 400,000 T food grain to Uzbeks.
newsitem.headline: Russia may barter 400,000 T food grain to Uzbeks.

text.p: Russia's Roskhleboprodukt grain trade agency is seeking government approval to barter 400,000 tonnes of domestic food grain to Uzbekistan for an unspecified amount of cotton, a Roskhleboprodukt source said on Wednesday.
The source, who declined to be identified, said that Russia would have a better harvest this year compared to last year's drought-hit output and that grain was available for export.
"We have a better harvest this year, so of course grain is available for export," he said.
Interfax news agency said the amount of raw cotton in question was 77,000 tonnes and that both sides were working on financing arrangements for the deal.
Russian government and independent officials have said that Russia is facing its second bad harvest in a row after last year's net 63.4 million tonnes, the worst in three decades.
Estimates for Russian grain output this year range from 68 million tonnes to 78 million tonnes.
Uzbekistan is the world's second largest cotton exporter and has forecast a flat cotton harvest this year of around 4.0 million tonnes of raw cotton.
The former Soviet republic had a grain harvest this year of 2.7 million tonnes, far below a targeted level of 4.5 million tonnes but above 1995's 2.38 million tonnes.
Uzbekistan needs about 3.5-4.0 million tonnes of food grains to meet annual demand.
